title: Conjecture 1.1
statement_text: A $d$-dimensional set of $n$ points determines at least $(d-1)n-O(d^{2})$ lines with pairwise distinct directions.
context_text: This conjecture is suggested in Brass, Moser, and Pach [4] (page 272), motivated by earlier related results of Jamison and of Blokhuis and Seress. The matching upper bound is witnessed by taking $n-d+1$ collinear points plus $d-1$ points in general position, giving $(d-1)(n-d+1)+\binom{d-1}{2}+1=(d-1)n-O(d^{2})$ distinct directions.
paper_contribution: Proves a weaker linear lower bound: any $d$-dimensional set of $n$ points determines at least $bdn$ lines with pairwise distinct directions for an absolute constant $b \geq \frac{1}{48}$, providing the first result linear in $dn$.
paper_title: Distinct Directions and Distinct Distances in $\mathbb{R}^d$

title: Conjecture 1.5
statement_text: For every fixed $d$ the following holds for all $d$-norms $\|\cdot\|$ but a meagre set. For all $n>n_{0}(d)$, any set of $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ that do not all lie in an affine hyperplane determine at least $(d-o(1))n$ distinct distances with respect to $\|\cdot\|$, where the $o(1)$-term tends to $0$ as $n$ tends to infinity.
context_text: A $d$-norm is a norm on $\mathbb{R}^d$; identifying a norm with its unit ball, the Hausdorff distance between unit balls (the largest distance from a point of one ball to the other ball) makes the space of $d$-norms a metric space, and it is a Baire space. A set of norms is nowhere dense if every non-empty open set contains a non-empty open set disjoint from it, and meagre if it is a countable union of nowhere dense sets; "all $d$-norms but a meagre set" thus means typical (generic) norms. Alon, Bucić and Sauermann proved that in all $d$-norms but a meagre set, any $n>n_0(d)$ points determine at least $(1-o(1))n$ distinct distances, which is tight because $n$ points in arithmetic progression on a line determine $n-1$ distances in every norm. Since that extremal example is one-dimensional, the conjecture concerns $d$-dimensional sets, i.e. sets not contained in an affine hyperplane. It is trivial for $d=1$ but open already for $d=2$. The authors prove that any $d$-dimensional set of $n$ points determines at least $bdn$ lines with pairwise distinct directions for an absolute constant $b\ge1/48$, and deduce the weaker bound of $(bd-o(1))n$ distinct distances for typical $d$-norms; they also note that $n-d+1$ points in arithmetic progression on a line plus $d-1$ further points in general position show the minimum is $\Theta(nd)$, and that a $(d-1)n-O(d^2)$ conjecture on distinct directions would give $(d-1-o(1))n$ distances. This is discrete geometry rather than graph theory.
paper_title: Distinct Directions and Distinct Distances in $\mathbb{R}^d$
